root_cause: an in-process cache in checkout-service grows without bound: entries are added and never evicted, so the resident set climbs steadily while the service keeps answering

evidence.observation: rose from 0.0 to 476.0, flat at zero through the baseline
evidence.supports: the cache never evicts - this is the mechanism
the resident set follows the cache, which ties the growth to it

evidence.observation: stayed at 0.0 for the whole window
evidence.supports: the database pool is untouched - the fault is in the process, not in its I/O

evidence.observation: went 0.1209 to 0.1506, inside its baseline range
evidence.supports: no dependency is slow or failing - a leak this early shows in memory before it shows in latency

ruled_out: connection pool exhaustion - db_pool_usage stayed at 0.0 throughout
a slow dependency - p95_by_dependency stayed inside its baseline range on both, among the metrics that stayed normal
an internal error in a dependency - no dependency_error or inventory_internal_error event appears, while cache_entries and memory_mb both rose
